links.outcome: Blinded clinician ratings of LLM discharge summaries vs physician-written on completeness, correctness, conciseness, trust
links.effect: LLM summaries had lower completeness (4.50 vs 5.00; p<0.001), similar correctness (p=0.14); trusted in 85.3%, partially trusted 11.6%, rejected 3.1% of cases.
links.quote: Physician-written summaries were trusted by both reviewers in 279 (95.5%) cases, whereas LLM-generated summaries were trusted in 249 (85.3%) cases, partially trusted in 34 (11.6%), and rejected in 9 (3.1%).

links.outcome: LLM-generated vs physician-written discharge summary quality scores
links.effect: Total scores did not differ (14.00 vs 14.00; p=0.34); LLM lower in completeness, greater in conciseness, similar correctness.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the quality (completeness, correctness, conciseness, trustworthiness) of LLM-generated discharge summaries compared to physician-written ones via a blinded retrospective/offline clinician reader study.
